In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection of the word “discourse” in a collaborative writing session indexes a variety of discoursal identities and that interaction constructs those identities.
the writers’ stances on discourse in this writing session index a range of discoursal identities and that interaction is a central component in the negotiation of those identities.
the discoursal identities that writers and readers develop about each other in the context of writing are shaped by the social interaction that occurs in writing sessions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
discoursal identities are constructed through the selection of words in texts, and through the embodied stances that writers take during collaborative writing.
we have demonstrated that the construction of discoursal identities is a complex, embodied, and situated process that occurs in interaction.
the writers’ stances on discourse index an array or array of identities that are negotiated and constructed through interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discoursal identity of the writer is a social construction that emerges from interaction.
the discoursal identity of academic writers is not only a product of individual agency but is also constructed in the context of group writing and social interaction.
the discursive construction of identity in academic writing is not a one-way street from writers to texts but a complex process of negotiation between writers and readers.
